claim.pdf_says: Format 4 (converting): INSPECT [ BACKWARD ] identifier-1 CONVERTING { identifier-6 / literal-4 } TO { identifier-7 / literal-5 } [ after-before-phrase ] - the printed figure has exactly TWO braces, each a balanced open/close pair spanning two stacked rows: the first encloses identifier-6 over literal-4, the second encloses identifier-7 over literal-5.
claim.markdown_says: Line 1: "<u>INSPECT</u> [ <u>BACKWARD</u> ] identifier-1 <u>CONVERTING</u> { identifier-6 } <u>TO</u> { identifier-7 } [ after-before-phrase ]"  Line 2 (an inline continuation built from a long run of ` ` padding): "...{ literal-4 ...{ literal-5 }"
claim.why_it_matters: The two-line inline rendering produces FOUR brace tokens with mismatched pairing: `{ identifier-6 }` and `{ identifier-7 }` are each closed on line 1, `{ literal-4` on line 2 opens a brace that is never closed at all, and `{ literal-5 }` reads as a third, separate brace group. A reader sees identifier-6 and literal-4 as belonging to different enclosures rather than as the two stacked alternatives of one brace; the unclosed `{ literal-4` is the same defect class already confirmed in CALL Format 2. The ` `-padded alignment also collapses in any non-fixed-width renderer, so the visual pairing is not recoverable.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on both sides, and the defect is worse than claimed. PDF (rendered spec_p673.png at 300dpi, printed page 643, cropped and 2x-upscaled over the Format 4 line): I read the glyphs directly. The Format 4 figure is 'INSPECT [ BACKWARD ] identifier-1 CONVERTING' followed by exactly TWO brace enclosures. Each is a single balanced open/close pair of PLAIN curly braces (no choice indicators - no vertical bars, no doubled/serifed choice glyphs) spanning two stacked rows: brace 1 holds identifier-6 on the upper row over literal-4 on the lower row; then the underlined word TO; then brace 2 holds identifier-7 over literal-5; then '[ after-before-phrase ]'. Plain braces = select exactly one of the two stacked alternatives at each position. MARKDOWN (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 27786-27787, byte-verified with cat -A): matches the claim's quote verbatim. Programmatic analysis after stripping tags and expanding  : line 1 has 2 '{' and 2 '}'; line 2 has 2 '{' and only 1 '}'. Combined the figure has FOUR '{' against THREE '}' - literally unbalanced, so `{ literal-4` is opened and never closed, exactly as claimed. This is not mere formatting or line wrapping: brace pairing is the normative syntactic notation of an ISO general format, and the markdown's pairing asserts a different syntax than the page prints - `{ identifier-6 }` reads as a required singleton group in which literal-4 is NOT an alternative. THREE additional facts make the claim's severity understated rather than overstated. (1) The alignment fails even in a fixed-width renderer: line 1's braces sit at columns 46 and 66, line 2's at columns 70 and 92 - off by 24 and 26 columns respectively, so the '2D stack' the   padding is imitating never lines up at all. (2) The two lines are NOT inside a code fence (the fence at line 27791 belongs to the following tallying-phrase figure) and line 1 has neither a trailing two-space hard break nor a
. Under CommonMark the soft line break therefore COLLAPSES the two source lines into a single rendered line, so `{ literal-4 ... { literal-5 }` renders trailing AFTER `[ after-before-phrase ]`, fully detached from the identifiers they alternate with - the stacked relationship is destroyed, not merely misaligned. (3) The correct transcription pattern already exists on this same page: the tallying-phrase figure immediately below is rendered as a fenced 2D block using box-drawing brace glyphs plus a prose 'Figure notes' block, so Format 4's inline rendering is an in-page inconsistency, not house style. Refutation attempts that failed: the text is not merely reflowed (the brace count itself differs, 4/3 vs the printed 2/2); it is not page-break furniture or hyphenation; it does change meaning. The only mitigation found is downstream prose - Syntax Rules 3, 4 and 9 of 14.9.22 do reference literal-4 and literal-5 as legitimate operands, so a diligent reader could reconstruct the intent - but that mitigates consequence, not the fact that the normative general-format figure is transcribed with wrong and unbalanced brace structure.
verdict.corrected_description: Page 673, INSPECT Format 4 (converting) general format. PDF prints TWO plain (non-choice) brace enclosures, each balanced and each spanning two stacked rows: { identifier-6 over literal-4 } TO { identifier-7 over literal-5 }, followed by [ after-before-phrase ]. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:27786-27787 flattens this into an unfenced two-source-line inline approximation containing FOUR '{' against THREE '}': `{ identifier-6 }` and `{ identifier-7 }` are closed on line 1, while line 2 (69 leading  ) contributes an unclosed `{ literal-4` and a spurious standalone `{ literal-5 }`. Beyond the mispairing described in the original claim, the   padding does not align even in monospace (braces at columns 46/66 on line 1 versus 70/92 on line 2), and because the block is not fenced and line 1 carries no hard break, CommonMark joins the two lines into one rendered line - placing `{ literal-4 ... { literal-5 }` after `[ after-before-phrase ]` and destroying the stacked-alternative relationship entirely rather than merely degrading it. Fix by transcribing Format 4 the same way the tallying-phrase figure on the same page already is: a fenced 2D block with box-drawing brace glyphs plus a Figure notes paragraph recording that both enclosures are plain braces (exactly one alternative selected from each).
